Through the open doorway of the first house, a hearth of large, carefully stacked logs still burns with a steady glowing fire. In the two other houses, only cold grey ashes of small dry twigs remain. Three men coming back from the fields at the end of the day: one stands calm and proud in the warm firelight of the burning hearth, the two others stare at their dead ashes. Beyond the village, the dark forest and a misty river; far below, the Atlantic Ocean catches the last light. A young Bakweri woman of about sixteen walks in the centre of the scene, modestly dressed in a long skirt and a wrap covering her chest, both made of fresh green fern fronds rubbed with red camwood powder, her arms and face dusted with red camwood. She is tied at the middle of a long rope: a group of women holds the rope in front of her, another group of women holds it behind her, and they walk her slowly through the village between traditional houses, singing. Faces solemn and proud, a sense of ritual passage, not of captivity. Villagers watch respectfully from the doorways. Volcano slopes and forest in the background. A dignified elderly African woman, Ki Wom, stands before a young man, Mban, who stands firm and upright: she rests her right hand on his head and with the other hand pours water over him from a fresh round calabash; the water catches the light as it falls. Beside them, an older man with a calm, wise face, Ngog, the father of the group, watches in silence. In the half-darkness behind them, men, women and children of the group sit along the rock walls with closed, unseeing eyes. Simple garments of raffia and bark cloth. Atmosphere solemn, sacred, intimate. Behind Mban, in the dark passage, the silhouette of the old guide Ngog is fading away into the shadows of the rock. Simple garments of raffia and bark cloth. Atmosphere of initiation, revelation and calm power. prompt: Night at the foot of a huge grey granite rock rising above tall savanna grass, in a timeless past. The dark mouth of a cave opens in the rock. Across the whole entrance, a large, perfect, intact spider web glistens with dew in silver moonlight, the spider resting at its centre. Just behind the web, in the darkness of the cave, barely visible, exhausted African families huddle in silence, holding their breath. In the foreground, seen from behind, a group of pursuers with hooded, hidden faces holding torches have stopped in front of the untouched web, about to turn back. Tension, silence, a miracle of fragility. prompt: Grassfields savanna of western Cameroon, in a distant past, near a forested mountain. The very instant a race begins. On a long fallen tree trunk sit three royal siblings: a young woman, Mfom, still seated, calmly pressing down with her body the end of her brother's wrapped cloth; her tall athletic brother, Koumjouom, who has just leapt forward and is being pulled back and thrown off balance by his trapped cloth; and their brother Nchare, a short man with a big round belly, short legs and eyes shining like a panther's, charging forward head down. Less than a hundred metres ahead, in the tall grass, a single large flat stone waits. To the side, a young man, Njimongha, has just given the starting signal with his raised arm. A crowd of followers in raffia and woven cloth watches, breathless. Dynamic, slightly humorous but noble. Around him, seven companions, mature warriors and elders, each sit on one of the stones, solemn, their hands raised or placed on their knees as they swear the pact. Behind them, a small crowd of a few hundred people, men, women and children, stands in the grass and listens. Raffia garments, simple woven cloth, iron spears planted in the ground. prompt: The wide brown Sanaga River at the edge of the forest, late afternoon, in a distant past. Across the whole river, from one bank to the other, lies what looks like an enormous dark tree trunk risen from under the water, wet and glistening, its surface subtly patterned like the scales of a gigantic python, though no head is visible. A long line of Beti families walks across it in single file: mothers carrying babies on their backs, elders guided step by step, men holding their spears upside down with the rounded end of the shaft resting on the trunk and the iron point raised away from it, baskets and bundles on their heads. On the near bank, two guardians watch the crossing. Atmosphere: awe, silence, fragile hope. prompt: Night over the wide Sanaga River in a distant past. The living bridge across the river is revealing itself: what everyone took for a giant tree trunk is twisting and rolling, and the immense body of a python rises from the black water, its scales lit in orange by burning bamboo torches. Sparks from a dropped torch fall on its back. People who were crossing lose their balance and fall into the river; on the far southern bank, those who already crossed reach out in horror; on the northern bank, families who had not yet stepped on the bridge stand frozen, torches raised. Dramatic but not gory: fear, separation, the moment a people is split in two. prompt: Dawn on the bank of a wide African river at the edge of savanna and forest, in a distant past. An elderly ancestor, Aso Abanda, stands at the water's edge, striking the surface of the river with a carved magic staff; rings of light spread from the point of impact. Above the river, a luminous rainbow arcs down from the sky and lays itself across the water from bank to bank, and where it touches the river it is turning into the long body of a great python, half light, half flesh. Behind the ancestor, his people, exhausted from their flight, with baskets, children and elders, watch in wonder. Mystical, majestic, hopeful. A colossal giant, an ancient Sao man as tall as a palm tree, kneels in the wide river and blocks its whole width with his enormous hands to catch fish, the water piling up against his palms. In his thick hair, nests of birds of prey; startled flocks of birds burst from the trees along the bank as he shouts. His bow, made from an entire palm trunk, lies on the bank. Tiny human figures and a fortified earthen town on a low mound in the distance show the scale. Legendary, majestic, not monstrous. At her feet lie the objects found on the rise: a stone, weapons, a helmet, a fishing harpoon, a staff of command and a copper necklace.
